package_info.why_malicious: A critical vulnerability (CVE-2022-24828) in Composer allowed attackers to achieve remote code execution on the Packagist.org repository infrastructure. This enabled attackers to tamper with package metadata and dependency resolution, causing Composer clients to download and execute attacker-controlled code during package installation or update, resulting in potential compromise of millions of PHP projects and servers.

execution_context.trigger: During Composer package install or update operation
execution_context.file_location: Packagist.org repository server-side dependency resolution logic (not present in user packages; exploit occurs in repository infrastructure)
required_permissions: network (to serve manipulated metadata and payloads)
filesystem (to modify or inject malicious package files)
environment_vars (to access server-side configuration and secrets)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Remote code execution was achieved by exploiting a vulnerability in the way Composer handled package metadata and dependency resolution. By submitting specially crafted package metadata to Packagist.org, an attacker could execute arbitrary PHP code on the repository server. This allowed the attacker to modify package metadata or binaries, redirecting Composer clients to download malicious dependencies. (Exact exploit code is not publicly disclosed in the report.)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During Composer package install or update operation, the attacker exploits a vulnerability in Packagist's server-side dependency resolution logic, submits crafted package metadata, which is processed by the server, resulting in arbitrary PHP code execution on the repository. This enables the attacker to manipulate package metadata and serve malicious dependencies to Composer clients, leading to remote code execution on downstream user servers.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Remote code execution on a central package repository is highly suspicious because it allows attackers to inject arbitrary code into any downstream project using Composer, enabling mass compromise.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, package repositories are expected to serve only authentic, verified package metadata and code. In this case, the repository's logic was subverted to serve attacker-controlled payloads, violating the trust model of the package ecosystem.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use involves serving updated or patched packages and metadata, but never arbitrary code execution or unauthorized modification of package metadata or binaries.
key_indicators: Remote code execution vulnerability in Packagist.org infrastructure
Manipulation of package metadata or dependency resolution logic
Composer clients receiving modified or malicious package metadata
Unexpected changes in package download URLs or dependency trees
Potential for mass downstream compromise via trusted supply chain

attack_chain.action: Attacker exploits CVE-2022-24828 in Packagist.org to achieve remote code execution on the repository server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains control over package metadata and dependency resolution logic.

attack_chain.action: Attacker modifies package metadata or binaries on Packagist.org, causing Composer clients to receive malicious dependencies during install or update.
attack_chain.leads_to: Downstream users unknowingly install attacker-controlled or backdoored packages.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes on user servers as part of the Composer install/update process, enabling data exfiltration, configuration modification, or persistence.
attack_chain.leads_to: Widespread compromise of PHP applications and infrastructure via the supply chain.

behavioral_signatures: Composer client receives unexpected changes in package metadata or download URLs from Packagist.org
Composer installs packages from non-standard, previously unseen, or attacker-controlled sources
Sudden appearance of new or modified dependencies in the dependency tree during install/update
Unexplained changes in the resolved package versions or sources
file_indicators: Unauthorized or unexpected files appearing in vendor/ directories after Composer operations
composer.lock or composer.json files modified to include suspicious or untrusted package sources
Presence of package source URLs or references not matching official Packagist domains
network_indicators: Composer client making HTTP(S) requests to unfamiliar or attacker-controlled domains during install/update
Unusual outbound connections from build or deployment servers during or immediately after Composer operations
Connections to domains or IPs not associated with official Packagist infrastructure
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Composer install and update operations for unexpected changes in package sources, metadata, or dependency trees. Alert on downloads from non-standard or untrusted domains, and on modifications to composer.json or composer.lock that introduce suspicious sources. Use file integrity monitoring on vendor/ directories and Composer manifest files. Correlate with network logs to detect outbound connections to unfamiliar domains during package installation. Regularly audit SBOMs and verify package signatures where available to ensure package integrity.
